claims.quote: I feel that we are but beginning the list. And we know now that the atom, that once we thought hard and impenetrable, and indivisible and final and—lifeless—lifeless, is really a reservoir of immense energy.
claims.description: Predicts that radioactive decay is a general property of all elements, and that atoms contain immense stored energy.

claims.quote: in the atoms in this bottle there slumbers at least as much energy as we could get by burning a hundred and sixty tons of coal.
claims.description: Quantifies the energy locked in a small quantity of uranium as equivalent to a hundred and sixty tons of coal.

claims.quote: If at a word, in one instant I could suddenly release that energy here and now it would blow us and everything about us to fragments;
claims.description: Imagines instantaneous release of the energy in atoms as an explosive force able to destroy a lecture hall and its surroundings.

claims.quote: we should not only be able to use this uranium and thorium; not only should we have a source of power so potent that a man might carry in his hand the energy to light a city for a year, fight a fleet of battleships, or drive one of our giant liners across the Atlantic;
claims.description: Predicts a compact atomic power source that could light a city for a year or propel a battleship fleet or ocean liner.

claims.quote: but we should also have a clue that would enable us at last to quicken the process of disintegration in all the other elements, where decay is still so slow as to escape our finest measurements.
claims.description: Speculates that the radioactive decay rate can be artificially accelerated in all elements.

claims.quote: Then that perpetual struggle for existence, that perpetual struggle to live on the bare surplus of Nature’s energies will cease to be the lot of Man.
claims.description: Predicts that abundant atomic energy will end humanity's struggle for subsistence and begin a new civilisation.

claims.quote: I see the desert continents transformed, the poles no longer wildernesses of ice, the whole world once more Eden. I see the power of man reach out among the stars....
claims.description: Envisions atomic power transforming deserts and polar regions into habitable land and enabling human travel to the stars.

claims.quote: was solved by a wonderful combination of induction, intuition, and luck by Holsten so soon as the year 1933.
claims.description: Artificially induced radioactivity in heavy elements is achieved by a scientist in 1933.

claims.quote: He set up atomic disintegration in a minute particle of bismuth; it exploded with great violence into a heavy gas of extreme radio-activity, which disintegrated in its turn in the course of seven days, and it was only after another year’s work that he was able to show practically that the last result of this rapid release of energy was gold.
claims.description: Induced atomic disintegration of bismuth releases energy and ultimately transmutes it into gold.

claims.quote: It was in 1953 that the first Holsten-Roberts engine brought induced radio-activity into the sphere of industrial production, and its first general use was to replace the steam-engine in electrical generating stations.
claims.description: Atomic engines are introduced industrially in 1953, replacing steam engines in electrical power stations.

claims.quote: Allowing for lubrication the Dass-Tata engine, once it was started cost a penny to run thirty-seven miles, and added only nine and quarter pounds to the weight of the carriage it drove.
claims.description: A lightweight, extremely cheap atomic engine powers automobiles and aircraft.

claims.quote: it was at last possible to add Redmayne’s ingenious helicopter ascent and descent engine to the vertical propeller that had hitherto been the sole driving force of the aeroplane without overweighting the machine, and men found themselves possessed of an instrument of flight that could hover or ascend or descend vertically and gently
claims.description: Atomic power enables hovering, vertical-takeoff aeroplanes combining helicopter and propeller engines.

claims.quote: in France alone in the year 1943 thirty thousand of these new aeroplanes were manufactured and licensed, and soared humming softly into the sky.
claims.description: Mass production and private ownership of atomic-powered aeroplanes, thirty thousand in one year in France.

claims.quote: atomic smelting was embarked upon so eagerly as to lead to a number of disastrous explosions due to inexperienced handling of the new power,
claims.description: Atomic power is applied to metal smelting, causing accidental explosions.

claims.quote: The coal mines were manifestly doomed to closure at no very distant date, the vast amount of capital invested in oil was becoming unsaleable, millions of coal miners, steel workers upon the old lines, vast swarms of unskilled or under-skilled labourers in innumerable occupations, were being flung out of employment
claims.description: Atomic power causes collapse of coal and oil industries and mass unemployment.

claims.quote: gold was undergoing headlong depreciation, all the securities upon which the credit of the world rested were slipping and sliding, banks were tottering, the stock exchanges were scenes of feverish panic;
claims.description: Atomic-derived gold supply and industrial disruption trigger worldwide financial panic and bank instability.

claims.quote: In the year 1955 the suicide rate for the United States of America quadrupled any previous record. There was an enormous increase also in violent crime throughout the world.
claims.description: Social dislocation from atomic energy causes a quadrupling of US suicides and a worldwide crime surge.

claims.quote: the revolutionary cheapening of both materials and electricity made the entire reconstruction of domestic buildings a matter merely dependent upon a reorganisation of the methods of the builder and the house-furnisher.
claims.description: Cheap atomic power makes the wholesale rebuilding of houses economically feasible.

claims.quote: In three years the frightful armoured monsters that had hooted and smoked and thundered about the world for four awful decades were swept away to the dealers in old metal, and the highways thronged with light and clean and shimmering shapes of silvered steel.
claims.description: Atomic-engined light vehicles rapidly replace petrol/alcohol automobiles within three years.

claims.quote: Government was a treaty, not a design; it was forensic, conservative, disputatious, unseeing, unthinking, uncreative; throughout the world, except where the vestiges of absolutism still sheltered the court favourite and the trusted servant, it was in the hands of the predominant caste of lawyers,
claims.description: Portrays mid-twentieth-century world government as unprepared and lawyer-dominated, contrasted with a later designed system of government.

claims.quote: Holsten, before he died, was destined to see atomic energy dominating every other source of power,
claims.description: Atomic energy will come to dominate all other power sources within the discoverer's lifetime.

claims.quote: the same perpetual miracle of motors dodging through it harmlessly, escaping headlong into the country from the Sabbatical stuffiness behind and below them.
claims.description: Imagines 1930s London still dominated by motor traffic, with the Heath Street area being rebuilt in Neo-Georgian style.

claims.quote: a women’s suffrage meeting—for the suffrage women had won their way back to the tolerance, a trifle derisive, of the populace again
claims.description: Predicts that the women's suffrage movement regains public tolerance by 1933.
